question.problem: Let $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and let $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ be a linear transformation. Find $[\,T\,]_{B}\,$ if $\,T({b}_{1})={b}_{2}\,$ and $\,T({b}_{2})=2{b}_{1}.$
question.worked_solution:
Since we have $\,T({b}_{1})={b}_{2}\,$ and $\,T({b}_{2})=2{b}_{1}\,$, we have

$$
[T({b}_{1})]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,[T({b}_{2})]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, the $B$-matrix for $T$ is a matrix  whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1})$ and $T({b}_{2})$ relative to the basis $B.$ Therefore, we obtain

$$
[\,T\,]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$
